Purpose and exclusions

Authored configuration for Consumables, tools and item-use effects. Runtime state never resides on this instance.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Select DA_Item_HealingDraught in Content Browser; set DefinitionId to a stable domain ID, then set the fields in the linked feature contract.
  2. Assign this instance to the consuming native owner through its Blueprint child/defaults or catalog; a content file that is never assigned has no runtime effect.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Author and validate stable definition/frame/field identity before use; load through declared references at readiness.
  2. Consumers may cache read-only references for their world/session lifetime; do not mutate the shared definition or place player quantities on it.
  3. On reimport/version change validate compatibility and migrate persistent IDs deliberately. Missing required rules fail closed; missing cosmetic layers use documented fallback.
  4. World/pawn teardown releases runtime references; persistent records retain IDs and versions only. Reconnect resolves the same definition without replaying grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Consumables, tools and item-use effects. Rule owner: URPGItemUseComponent. This asset’s role is Authored configuration for Consumables, tools and item-use effects. Runtime state never resides on this instance.

  1. Player activates a hotbar item reference; server resolves actual ownership and use definition, validates target/alive state/cooldown and reserves the action.
  2. Backend atomically consumes the stack quantity or durability and records a use entitlement/receipt with the accepted effect parameters.
  3. Zone applies the live effect once using receipt ID and current avatar-life binding; never let a replayed receipt heal a later respawned body again.
  4. To close a crash gap, persist the chosen consumable recovery policy: on uncertain effect application during zone crash, restore the durable post-use resource snapshot or reconcile entitlement before enabling the next avatar. Do not simply consume in SQL then forget the effect.
  5. Publish owner inventory/resource updates and cosmetic cue from the accepted result. A non-economic gather tool check does not itself consume a tool unless the action's terminal policy says so.
  6. On transfer, drain/reconcile item-use commands before snapshot; long cooldown expiry follows the durable cooldown policy.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / PotionStack_A / Character_A at 40 health. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Same use packet twice -> one item consumed and one 30-health application.
Potion missing or stack replaced -> ItemMissing/StaleItem, no heal.
Use while dead -> TargetInvalid before commit.
Crash after consumption before live effect -> explicit entitlement/resource recovery, not silent loss or duplicate heal.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not put mutable stock, current health, inventory quantities or player quest progress on a shared Data Asset. A soft reference still needs validation and readiness.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
